newsitem.title: BULGARIA: NATURAL GAS DEMAND ON BALKANS TO RISE BY YEAR 2010.
newsitem.headline: NATURAL GAS DEMAND ON BALKANS TO RISE BY YEAR 2010.

text.p: Bulgarian-Russian joint gas stock company Topenergy said on Wednesday it envisaged a significant increase in natural gas demand on the Balkan until 2010 achieving 36-37 billlion cubic metres per year.

Demand forecasts on the Balkans exclude Romania, Bosnia, Croatia and Slovenia, Topenergy's Galina Pavlova said in a report at a meeting of the European Union's Energy Centre on natural gas infrastructure development in Bulgaria.
Topenergy, in which Russia's gas giant Gazprom holds a 50-percent stake, is planned to sell and deliver Russian gas to the Balkans via Bulgaria.
"Plans are to transit Russian natural gas through the territory of Romania and via Bulgaria it will be distributed...to the borders of Turkey, Greece, Macedonia and Serbia," the report said.

Topenergy plans annual supplies of Russian gas in 2010 of 20 billion cubic metres for Turkey, four billion cubic metres for Greece, one billion cubic metres for Albania, two billion cubic metres for Serbia and one billion cubic metres for Macedonia, Pavlova said.
The Bulgarian government is expected in mid-October to award a concession for the construction of pipelines to Topenergy, which was established in May last year.

Sasho Donchev, who is on Topenergy board and also an executive direator of Bulgaria's private gas distribution firm Overgas pointed out that with its geographical position Bulgaria had great chances "to become a transitting gas corridor from Russia to the Balkans and Italy".

Bulgaria has a 2,200-km-long pipeline network, which includes 625 km of transit pipelines. But Topenergy needs to enlarge the transit pipeline to 1,300 km until 2010 and build also 240-megawatts compressor stations in order to meet the growing demand of the Balkan countries, Pavlova said.
The joint firm plans to increase the Bulgarian distribution system from 17 billion cubic metres to some 30 billion cubic metres.
Topenergy will also build gas storage facilities in Bulgaria in the next 10-15 years with a capacity of 3.5-4 billion cubic metres in order to ensure constant gas supplies to the Balkan countries.
Bulgaria has its Chiren gas storage facility in northern Bulgaria.
